config.else: Lumen is both drawn and wrecked

config.label: fifteen feet of broken manacle chain
a finger bone, filed to a point
a brass lamp, half full of oil
Lumen, the holy sword of the Dawn
Someone named Abelard died in the pit. He scratched a line of the Host’s rhyme into the wall.
Abelard of the Dawn swore the lich would never have his own blade. “He gave it to the deep.”
The far door of the Ossuary is bolted on the Ossuary side.
A glyph is only a ring. Break the ring and it’s just paint.
The Scriptorium carpet sags in the middle.
The statues move only when nothing is looking at them.
The rod through the orrery’s sun has a Dawn hilt. It is Lumen, which drinks any spell that strikes it.
Cantrips die as they near the rod in the orrery.
The orrery’s sun is warm, and it beats. The Host keeps a mirror on it day and night.
First the breath went, then the warmth, and last, sleep.
and the sun for the grave.
A spell of weight, carved under the lectern.
Ser Eldric of the Long Watch
Get out of the Ninefold Cell

header.label: a snap of heat and light at a point you can see
frost on a surface, or a mouthful of water turned to ice
one breath of wind, enough to snuff a candle across a room
knits a small break: a torn page, a cracked pin, a split lip
an unseen pull on something lighter than a book, within sight
swallows one sound for a moment
flame, fanned, then lit into a lance
a shell of ice that heals its own cracks

other.text: shields target from the next spell

header.label: rimes a mirror over until it shows nothing
a swallowed sound, carried, then let go at once
ties the hour back on itself
makes one thing very, very heavy, for one breath
Lord of the first light, give us the hour back.

then.text: Nine rooms, two guests, one door. I made every lock myself.
How touching. The thief and the paladin.
Shh. Some of us are working.
I do like to keep an eye on my children.
I’m getting bored. Have you tried oil? Oil is very good for rust.
The rhyme, you dolts. I hum it for a reason.
Both of you? In the pit? Oh, this is embarrassing. Here.

paragraphs: The cart stopped at the bottom of the world, and a voice like a delighted host said, “Ah. Guests.”

They took Roland Vey’s picks, his knives and his good boots. They took Ser Eldric’s sword, his mail and the sun from his surcoat. They did not take the argument the two of them had been having since the road, which Roland was winning.
“Nine rooms,” said the Hollow Host, from every mirror at once. “One door. I made every lock myself, and I do so love to watch. Die as often as you like. I’ll put you back.”

body.label: Wake as Roland, in the pit

header.label: a knight’s skeleton in a rotted surcoat

header.inquest: The grate is too heavy for anything you can do from down here.
Look past the grate. On the far door above, something only needs to slide.

paragraphs: You wake on your back at the bottom of a stone throat twelve feet deep. The sky is an iron grate.
The oubliette: twelve feet of wet stone, and a grate for a lid.
A pipe in the wall drips into a drain. In the corner sits a skeleton in a rotted surcoat, head tilted, as if waiting for someone to finish a story.
Eldric’s chain hangs from the grate, swaying.
Water is roaring out of the pipe. It’s already past your knees.

body.label: Read the scratches by the skeleton
Tug the bolt across the room
Tug the peg out from under the sluice lever
Throw the chain up and hook the grate
Boost Roland up to the grate

paragraphs: Under the ribs, a finger bone has been filed to a point against the stone, patiently, over what must have been weeks. It’s a very good pick. You take it, and say thank you, because someone should.

The surcoat was white once, with a rising sun. You know the signet: Abelard of the Dawn, who rode against the Hollow Host forty years ago carrying the order’s holy sword, and never came back. The songs say he swore the lich would never have his own blade. “He gave it to the deep.”
Tally marks, hundreds of them, and under them one line cut deep: FLAME FOR THE FOOL. HE HUMS IT WHEN HE’S PLEASED.
The rest is scraped away, or was never written. Whoever cut it stopped mid-word.
Through the bars: a room of bones, a long lever propped up by a wooden peg, and on the far door, an iron bolt shot home on this side.
A bolt is a small thing. It doesn’t need lifting. It needs sliding.

header.source: retell: "From the bottom of the pit, Roland drew a bolt across the room with a crook of two fingers."

paragraphs: You crook two fingers and pull. Across the room above, the bolt grates, sticks, and slides free.
From beyond that door, Eldric’s voice: “…Was that you?”

header.source: retell: "Roland climbed the knight’s chain out of the pit, and for once said nothing clever."

paragraphs: Hand over hand, up fifteen feet of chain that held Eldric to a pillar an hour ago. At the top a big hand closes on your wrist and hauls.
“Thank you,” you say, and find you mean it. Eldric looks as surprised as you are.
Third throw. The chain wraps a bar of the open grate and bites. Not dignified, but it holds.
Roland stands on your shoulders, then on your hands, then is gone over the lip. “I’ll fetch the chain,” he calls down. “Don’t go anywhere.”

header.label: the sluice lever
a rusted lever by the portcullis

header.inquest: Rust can be broken, or it can be eased.
There’s lamp oil in this prison. A rusted lever forced once is forced for good.

paragraphs: Bones line the walls in niches, sorted by size with terrible care. An iron grate is set in the floor. A long sluice lever is propped up by a wooden peg. By the north arch, a rusted lever stands beside a lowered portcullis.
The east door stands unbolted.
The east door is bolted on this side.

body.label: Let your chain down into the pit
Draw the bolt on the east door

paragraphs: You get your fingers under the bars and stand up. The grate comes with you, shrieking, and you lean it against the bones.
The grate lifts a finger’s width and drops. It wants a stronger back.
You pay the chain out over the edge until it hangs within reach of the bottom, and brace your feet.
“That’s my exit,” says a voice below. “I take back half of what I said in the cart.” “Only half?” “Let’s see how the climb goes.”
You draw the bolt. It was never meant to be hard from this side.

header.source: retell: "The sluice opened, and the Well of the Eye drained away into the pit below."

paragraphs: The peg flies, the lever drops, and somewhere under the floor a great throat of water opens. Next door, the well begins to drain. The pipe in the pit begins to roar.
Below the grate, Roland, very calmly: “Eldric. Eldric. I have made a mistake.”
You haul. The lever moves an inch, then all at once, and snaps off in your fist. The portcullis rattles up into the ceiling and stays there.
It doesn’t move. Rust holds it like a grudge.
The rust drinks the oil with a faint hiss.
The lever swings sweetly. The portcullis climbs into the dark.
The portcullis drops with a crash that shakes dust from the skulls.

header.label: an altar of the Dawn, overturned
a ring of red sigils across the north threshold

header.inquest: That ring of paint is the trap. Rings can be broken.
The paint’s still wet. Scrape it, or freeze it.

paragraphs: You wake against a pillar with your wrists in iron. The chain runs to a ring sunk in the stone, rusted, but as thick as your thumb.

A chapel of the Dawn, or it was. The altar lies on its face. Someone has painted a grinning mouth over the sunburst on the wall. The west door is shut fast. The north door stands open, but across its threshold runs a ring of red sigils.
The ring of sigils is cut through with a long scrape.
Frost furs the sigils.

body.label: Tear the ring out of the pillar
Scrape through the ring with your chain

header.source: retell: "Eldric pulled the iron ring out of the pillar, stone and all."

paragraphs: You set your feet against the pillar and lean back until your shoulders crack. The stone gives first. The ring comes out with a fist of rock still on it, and now you have fifteen feet of chain and nobody holding the other end.
Two kicks. The bolt tears out of the far side and the door slams open onto a room full of bones.
The door shudders in its frame and holds.
The paint is still tacky. Whoever drew this did it recently, and badly. A glyph is only a ring with opinions: break the ring and it’s just paint.
Wardens of the Dawn are taught this before they’re taught to ride: a glyph is a ring. Cut the ring.
You drag the chain’s end across the threshold. The ring of sigils splits with a sound like a struck match that doesn’t catch.
Frost spreads over the red paint until the sigils go dull and grey. It won’t last past the turn.
You set your shoulder to it and the altar rolls upright with a boom that rings through every room. On top, a candle stub, cold.
It doesn’t budge.
A snap of your fingers. The candle catches and stands up very straight.

header.source: retell: "Eldric kept vigil at the defiled altar, and Roland, who believes in nothing he can’t pick, knelt beside him."

paragraphs: You kneel. For a long moment there is only the drip of water and the mouth painted on the wall. Then the candle stands up taller, as if someone had opened a window onto morning.
Roland, who believes in nothing he can’t pick, is kneeling too. He looks embarrassed about it. You don’t say anything. That seems like the kind thing.
The sigils light as you cross. Fire comes up out of the floor like a held breath let go.
It is very fast, and you are very small.
You come through it with your hair smoking and a burn down one arm.

header.label: the lectern
the Host’s day-book, written backwards
the lectern’s top, one slab of black stone the size of a coffin lid

header.inquest: Stone that heavy hides something underneath.
The writing runs backwards, like writing in a mirror. And he kept that slab where only a strong man could show it to you.

paragraphs: Shelves climb to the ceiling, and the air smells of paper slowly going to dust. A long red carpet runs from the door to a lectern of black stone at the far end. A lamp hangs on a hook by the door.
The carpet sags in the middle, just slightly, like a hammock.
Eldric is holding the lectern slab up on his shoulders, red in the face.

body.label: Edge along the shelves to the lectern
Tell Eldric to keep to the shelves
Pick the lock on the north door

paragraphs: Halfway down, the carpet gives under you like a held breath. You drop through a hatch and down a long slick chute, and land, hard, at the bottom of the pit you started in.
You saw it sag. You walked down it anyway. There’s a lesson here, and the Host is already laughing it at you.
Sideways, along the shelves, past a thousand spines. The carpet sags as you pass it, empty.
A brass lamp, half full of oil. Light enough to carry, heavy enough to be useful.
Every line runs right to left, every letter backwards. You read it the way you’d read a forger’s mirror-copy: slowly, and with a certain professional admiration.
“Year one of forever. The breath went first; I didn’t miss it. Then the warmth, which I did. And last, sleep. I have not slept since, so I built a game to pass the nights.”
In the margin, a doodle of a man stepping into a mirror, and four words: A BLINK FOR THE BOLD.
The slab comes up off its column with a grinding groan and settles on your shoulders. Something is carved on its underside.
You squint at it upside down. Wizard’s scrawl. It means nothing to you, and you can’t hold this forever.

header.source: retell: "Eldric held up a slab no two men should lift, while Roland read the spell carved under it."

paragraphs: Carved where only a strong man could show it to you: a spell of weight. Three words, and a thing becomes, for one breath, very, very heavy. You read it twice, then once more for luck.
“Done?” says Eldric, through his teeth. “Done.” The slab comes down like a door slammed by a god.
The lock is old and proud of itself. The finger bone teaches it humility.
The door comes off its hinges, and its frame comes with it.
The door holds. Your shoulder doesn’t thank you.

header.label: the Great Eye
the bottom of the well

header.inquest: Something down there wants fetching. Water can be dived, or let out.
The pit you started in had a pipe. The sluice in the Ossuary decides where this water goes.

paragraphs: The middle room. A round shaft fills most of the floor, with black water a long way down. On the north wall hangs the largest mirror you have ever seen, framed in bone: an eye with no lid. Stairs climb north. A door leads west. To the east, a ledge drops into darkness.
The well is dry. Far down, in the mud, something long and straight catches the light.
Far down, under the black water, something catches the light, and is gone.
A bronze shutter covers the Eye.

body.label: Anchor the chain and climb down

paragraphs: You look, and the Eye looks back, and you can’t look away. Somewhere in the glass, something is humming, very pleased with itself: “…and the sun for the grave.” When you can blink again, a long moment has gone.
A long moment, for a line of verse. You’d call it a fair trade if he hadn’t enjoyed it so much.
You loop the chain round the well-head and go down hand over hand into the cold.
The cold hits like a wall. You go down blind, find the mud, find a hilt, and come up with a sword and no feeling in your hands.
The cold closes your throat. You come up empty, coughing, with your heart pounding wrong.
A good plain longsword, under forty years of silt.
Abelard’s. He gave it to the deep, the songs said, and here it is: not lost, only hidden where a lich would never look. Down.
Up the chain, out of the cold.

header.label: the statue lever
the planet lever
the eye lever

header.inquest: Three carvings, three mirrors.
Close the right mirror and something in the Gallery stops being watched.

paragraphs: Racks of weapons, rusted to lace. Along the north wall stand three levers, each under a small carving: a statue, a planet, an open eye. The statue lever is red with rust. A spiral stair climbs into the dark. High on the west wall, a ledge overhangs, too high to reach. South, a door to the chapel.

Most of it is rust holding hands. But a soldier knows where to look: at the back of the third rack, a notched arming sword with sound steel under the scale. You take it, and your hand stops feeling empty.
Rust. Rust. A halberd that is mostly a rumour. Nothing you’d trust with your life, and you’d know.
Two rooms away, something slams. Or opens. You’d have to go and look.
Next door, bronze rings on bronze.
The lever comes down and keeps coming, and snaps. Far off, a shutter crashes shut. It’s staying shut.
The lever doesn’t move.
The rust drinks the oil and goes dark.
The lever swings. Up in the Gallery, a shutter slides.
Mend is for torn pages and split lips. Nobody told the lever that. The broken pin knits, a little crooked, and the lever swings again.

header.label: a round mirror aimed at the sun

header.inquest: The three planets move at different speeds.
Count how far each planet moves for one turn of the crank.

paragraphs: A brass orrery fills the room. At its heart hangs a sun the size of a man’s head, gleaming as if lit from inside. A bright rod pierces it top to bottom, and above the sun the rod ends in a short crossbar, like a crown. Three planets ride their rings: red Ember at
, blue Tide at
, gold Crown at
. A crank stands at the rim. A plaque is set in the base.
A round mirror on the wall is aimed at the sun, and nowhere else.
A bronze shutter covers a round mirror on the wall.
In the corner stands a stone Jester with a painted grin, one foot raised as if mid-dance.
The three planets kneel in one line. The rod through the sun stands a little proud of it.
The sun sits loose in its cradle, and it is beating.
The orrery is a wreck of bent rings. The rod is jammed through the middle of it, beyond anyone’s drawing.

body.label: Wrench the sun off its axle

paragraphs: WHEN THE WANDERERS KNEEL IN ONE LINE, THE AXIS MAY BE DRAWN.
Gears tick under the floor. Ember creeps to
. Tide swings to
. Crown sweeps round to
All three stop in a line, and something deep in the sun goes click.

That crossbar above the sun isn’t a crown. It’s a quillon. That is a hilt, and you know it: the white hilt of Lumen, the holy sword of your order, which drinks any spell that strikes it. They built the orrery around a sword.
It’s warm. Nothing heats it. Hold your hand close and it beats, slow as a sleeper’s heart.
A lich keeps his life somewhere outside his body. This one keeps a mirror on it day and night. You would too.
You flick a spark at the rod. It gutters as it gets close, and goes out, as if something drank it.

header.source: retell: "Eldric drew Lumen out of the orrery like a sword from a stone, because it was one."

paragraphs: It slides out of the sun like a sword from a scabbard, because it is one. Lumen is lighter than it looks and colder than it should be, and the edge has never been nicked. It knows your hand.
You take hold of the hilt, and it bites cold into your palm. It won’t come for you. Whatever this is, it wants a hand that prays.

header.source: retell: "They took the Hollow Host’s heart out of his orrery."

paragraphs: You lift the sun out of its cradle. It beats against your palms, slow, offended.
Every mirror in the prison turns to look at you.
Behind its shutter, the round mirror sees nothing at all.

header.source: retell: "Eldric tore the sun off its axle, and the Ninefold Cell began to fall."

paragraphs: You get both arms round the sun and heave. The rings bend, the rod bends, and the sun comes away with a sound like a bell thrown down a stair. Something inside it cracks. Every mirror in the prison screams, and dust begins to sift from the ceiling.

header.label: a tall black mirror facing the statues

header.inquest: The statues have moved before. Look at the floor.
They only dance when nothing’s looking. Something is always looking in here.

paragraphs: A long hall of plinths. On two stand statues: a Knight in stone plate, twice the size of a man, and a Widow in a stone veil with her hands half raised. The third plinth is empty. Arches open west and east, and stairs lead down.
A tall black mirror faces the statues from the south wall.
A bronze shutter covers the tall mirror on the south wall.
The Knight’s plinth stands empty.

body.label: Tell Eldric to push it with his eyes shut

paragraphs: Scuffs in the dust: long curved scrapes, plinth to arch and back again.

They’ve moved, and not by being dragged: the scrapes are footsteps. Yet they never move while you’re here, and that mirror never looks away from them. Statues that move only when nothing is watching. You’ve read about worse.
Someone’s been dragging furniture.
Your reflection, the statues behind it, and for half a heartbeat a tall paper man standing among them, smiling. Then just the statues.
You set your shoulder to the Knight and shove. It won’t move. It’s as if the stone is holding its breath while you look at it.

header.source: retell: "On Roland’s word, and against all sense, Eldric shut his eyes and pushed a stone knight through a wall of air."

paragraphs: “Shut my eyes,” Eldric says. He does. Nothing moves. “Something’s still watching it,” you realise aloud. The mirror.

“Shut my eyes,” Eldric says flatly. “And push.” He does. The Knight slides like a boat leaving the shore, through the arch, and onto the great pan before the Gate, which sinks under it with a groan of chains. Eldric opens his eyes, looks at what he did, and looks at you. You shrug: he did the pushing.

header.inquest: Each lock says what it wants.
His heart, his guardian, and what he gave up, in order.

paragraphs: The door is black iron, twice Eldric’s height, with no handle. Three locks are set in it: a socket shaped like a sun, a stone mouth with parted lips, and, on the floor before it, a great iron pan hung on chains like one side of a scale. Words are cut above each.
The stone Knight stands on the pan, which has sunk to the floor.
The Widow stands by the door, hands half raised, much closer than you left her.
The sun sits in its socket, beating.
The stone mouth is closed and smiling.

body.label: Read the words over the locks
Set the sun in its socket
Speak three cantrips into the mouth

paragraphs: Over the sun: ONLY MY HEART OPENS MY DOOR.
Over the mouth: GIVE BACK WHAT I GAVE FOR FOREVER, IN THE ORDER I GAVE IT.
Over the pan: LET A GUARDIAN OF STONE STAND HERE IN MY PLACE.
You both stand on it. The pan sinks two fingers’ width, and stops.
The pan sinks a finger’s width under you, and stops. It wants far more than a man.
The sun fits its socket exactly. Something behind the iron unlatches, and the heart goes on beating in the door.
The mouth takes your breath, then your warmth, then the small silence after, and its lips close with a click like a satisfied sigh.
The mouth laughs at you, and frost comes out of it.
The world folds up like a cheap theatre, and the Hollow Host claps.
You wake where you began: Roland in the pit, Eldric in chains, every lock relocked. Only what you learned came with you.
You wake on the threshold, with everything you carried out of the cells.
The door swings in on silence. Beyond it, a stair climbs toward candlelight.
Behind you, with a long tired roar, the Ninefold Cell finishes falling in.
“Well!” says the Host, from up the stair. “You think. I do like that in a guest. Come up.”
“Well,” says the Host, from up the stair. “You certainly hit things. Come up.”

header.source: pattern rhyme: flame, frost, blink, sunfall ~ repeat ~ one per round ~ recall first when hask.saw_heart and holder != nobody and not heart.cracked ~ falter instead of sunfall when holder != nobody and not heart.cracked
spell flame: at roland ~ then wound target 1 ~ blocked by shield, absorb, parry, interrupt ~ redirected by guard
spell frost: at eldric ~ then freeze target ~ kill target when target.frozen ~ blocked by shield, absorb, interrupt
spell blink: through mirror ~ then set hask.dodging: yes ~ then set hask.grounded: yes next round ~ fails when count(mirror, in: here, open: yes) == 0 or hask.pinned ~ on fail: set hask.grounded: yes
spell sunfall: at pov.all ~ then kill target ~ blocked by shield, absorb
spell recall: at holder ~ then take heart ~ blocked by shield, absorb, guard
spell falter: ~ then nothing
encounter hask ~ round by round ~ countdown 3s per act ~ plus 2s when inquest ~ timeout stay ~ hask casts last ~ until hask.wards == 0 or pov.all.down

header.label: the east mirror
the west mirror

paragraphs: A round room, all candles. Two tall mirrors face each other across it. A yard above the floor hangs the Hollow Host: a tall man made of very old paper, in a magister’s robe, with two coals for eyes and a smile he has clearly practised.
“Three wards,” he says, and touches the air around him. It rings like glass.
He looks at the cracked sun in your hands, and his smile thins. “Two, then. Vandals.”
You know his rhyme, every line. You know what he does first.

header.inquest: Watch his hands. They tell you what’s coming.
He’ll do what the rhyme says next. Answer it before he finishes.

paragraphs: He draws a line of red across the air with one finger.
Flame for the fool. He’s looking at Roland.
The floor rimes over, creeping toward Eldric.
Frost for the brave.
His eyes go to the mirrors: one, then the other.
A blink for the bold. Next round he’ll come out on foot.
He cups his hands, and the candlelight drains into them.
The sun for the grave. Anyone unshielded dies.
He holds out a hand toward his heart, palm up, like a man asking for his hat back.
He cups his hands, looks at his heart in your keeping, and lets the light go.
He is on the floor, on his own two feet, within reach of a sword.
Eldric is cased in ice to the shoulders.
Spark, gust, spark: a lance of fire, aimed with great care at your only friend. The ice goes to steam. “Warn me next time.” “I just did.”

header.source: shield target

paragraphs: Chill, mend, chill. Ice grows over
in a clear shell, sealing its own cracks as fast as they come.
Chill and gust: frost runs across
until it shows nothing at all.

header.source: interrupt hask when next in [flame, frost]

paragraphs: Hush, gust, spark: you gather a silence, throw it, and let it go all at once. The crack slaps every candle flat.
The Host flinches, and whatever he was weaving comes apart in his fingers.
He winces, but whatever he’s building is too big to drop.

header.source: pin hask

paragraphs: Three words of weight. The Host drops out of the air like a dropped cloak and hits the flagstones on his knees, very surprised, and very, very heavy.

header.source: skip hask this round when not hask.saw_heart

paragraphs: You hold up the brass sun. It beats in your hand.
The Host stops in the air. For the first time since the cart, he has nothing to say. “That’s— where did— that is mine.” For a whole breath he forgets to cast anything at all.
“Yes, yes, I saw you take it,” he says. “Do be careful with it.”
He isn’t there. The edge passes through a smear of old paper and candlelight.
Lumen lets go of everything it has drunk, all at once, down the length of one stroke. Two of his wards break together, like two windows in a storm.
Steel meets a ward, and the ward rings, and cracks, and falls away like a pane of glass.

header.source: guard roland ~ parry with abelard_sword ~ absorb with lumen

paragraphs: You step in front of Roland. Whatever comes for him will have to come through you.

header.source: absorb with lumen

paragraphs: You raise Lumen like a lamp in a dark room.
You put a fist, or a sword, through the nearest mirror. Glass rains. The Host makes a small hurt noise, as if you’d trodden on his foot.

header.source: retell: "Eldric set the Host’s heart on the flagstones and broke it under his heel."

paragraphs: You set the sun on the flagstones and bring your heel down. It breaks like a bell. The Host screams with every mirror in the room, and for the first time he looks like what he is: old paper, and nothing holding it together.
You toss Eldric the sun. He catches it one-handed, as if he’d been catching hearts all his life.

header.source: retell: "Roland poured an Ember Lance into Lumen, and Eldric cut the air in half."

paragraphs: Roland doesn’t aim at the lich. He aims at Eldric’s sword: spark, gust, spark, poured into the blade. Lumen drinks the lance and turns white, and Eldric cuts the air in half. The light goes where the edge points. The Host, floating, untouchable, is suddenly neither.
Fire takes Roland full in the chest.
Eldric takes the fire meant for Roland on his own chest, and staggers, and stays up.
Eldric turns the flame aside on Abelard’s blade, and it splashes harmless across the floor.
Ice climbs Eldric to the shoulders and holds him fast.
He steps into a mirror and out of the other, and lands on his feet, laughing.
He throws himself at the glass and hits frost, hard. He lands on the flagstones in a heap of robes.
Light, all of it, everywhere at once.
The heart leaps from your hand to his, like a dog called home.
The spell breaks on Roland’s ice and runs off it like rain off a window.
Lumen drinks the spell whole and begins to glow.
Nothing comes. The spell died in his hands.
Nothing. He will not burn his own heart, and he knows you know it.
The last ward breaks. The Hollow Host comes down out of the air like a kite with its string cut, and lies on the flagstones, and is suddenly very small.
Without his heart, there is nothing to put him back. He looks at the two of you with mild interest, says “Oh. Nicely done,” and comes apart into ash and old pages.
“You’ll want to do something about my heart,” he says, from the floor, with a little of his old cheer. “Or I’ll be back. I’m very patient.”

body.label: Carry it home to the Dawn together

paragraphs: They climbed out of the Host’s house at sunrise, a thief and a knight, both of them filthy, neither of them dead.
Eldric carried Lumen home to an order that had stopped hoping for it.
Roland, at the crossroads, offered his hand. Eldric looked at it for a long moment, the way you’d look at a lock, and took it.
Roland kept the heart. He told Eldric it was for study, and Eldric let him say it.
It sits in a box on Roland’s desk to this day, beating slowly, waiting. Some nights, when Roland reads late, he could swear it hums.

They carried the heart between them, a week on foot, to the first chapel of the Dawn they found, and laid it under the altar, and kept vigil over it a night and a day: the knight praying, the thief keeping the candle lit.
In the morning there was only brass, cold, and the beat had stopped.

header.source: retell: past tense ~ third person ~ by turn ~ skip examine when nothing learned ~ merge walk ~ one chapter per room, on first visit ~ fold deaths into “Again, and again.”

paragraphs: And the Host, who kept score, wrote in his day-book in a very small hand: CLEVER.
And the Host, who kept score, wrote in his day-book in a very small hand: STRONG. THEN CLEVER. EVENTUALLY.
